name: NetScaler RCE
tile_line: Exploited since September; patching won't evict intruders.
tldr: Anyone who can reach a Citrix NetScaler ADC or Gateway can run commands on it, no login, and default setups are affected. Exploited since September, on CISA's exploited list. If you run your own, update now; if you were late, check for a break-in.
summary: Attackers have used it since at least 20 Sep, and public exploit code came out on 28 Sep. Rapid7 found a web shell and an attacker command that archives the config, keys and certificates.

affected.label: A NetScaler you run yourself
affected.text: Customer-managed NetScaler ADC or Gateway, including Secure Private Access hybrid setups that use NetScaler instances. Citrix-managed cloud services and Adaptive Authentication are updated by Citrix's parent, Cloud Software Group.

affected.label: A build older than the fix
affected.text: 14.1 before 14.1-73.37, 13.1 before 13.1-64.23, 14.1-FIPS before 14.1-73.37 FIPS, or 13.1-FIPS/NDcPP before 13.1-37.279. The same builds fix CVE-2026-88772, a second bug attackers used at the same time.

affected.label: Attackers can send it web traffic
affected.text: Citrix lists "All deployments (default configuration)": no Gateway or AAA virtual server is needed. watchTowr says any endpoint that logs attacker-controlled web data can trigger it, including the management interface. Cloudflare says the Gateway must be publicly reachable; Citrix and watchTowr describe it more broadly.

do.label: Update to 14.1-73.46 or later
do.text: Go to 14.1-73.46, 13.1-64.29, 14.1-73.46 FIPS or 13.1.37.283, not just the first fix. These also fix CVE-2026-88779 (a crash bug, on CISA's exploited list since 4 Oct) and CVE-2026-107406 (SAML setups).

do.label: Late to patch? Assume a break-in
do.text: Patching doesn't remove an attacker who's already in. Mandiant says to end admin, Gateway, VPN and ICA sessions after patching, and to rotate admin passwords, SSH keys, TLS certificates and private keys, and the LDAP, RADIUS, TACACS, SNMP and API credentials the appliance uses. Follow Citrix's suspected-compromise steps, which include rebuilding the appliance.

do.label: Look for web shells
do.text: Unit 42 and Rapid7 found a web shell at `/var/netscaler/logon/LogonPoint/custom/.ctxs.receiver`. Mandiant's checks include whether `/bin/sh` has been made to run as root, and PHP handlers added to `/etc/httpd.conf`.

do.label: No workaround
do.text: Mandiant says disabling DTLS or blocking UDP 443 only helps against CVE-2026-88772, not this bug. A web firewall in front only covers the traffic that passes through it. Update.
